subject: dcar_proper:  nimEigen() has a complex eigenvalue.

messages.author: 2c82479e1954c509
messages.subject: dcar_proper:  nimEigen() has a complex eigenvalue.
parts:
Hi,

I am trying to use nimble to implement a logistic model with CAR model. I follow the example in the manual. The adjacent matrix I considered is based on a regular grid. When I set the grid as 4\times4, the model can be compiled, however, when the grid is larger, there is an error about nimEigen() in dcar_proper. Since I simulated the data from a car model, I think the model should work.

I downloaded the source files and found that when the size is larger, the function calculating the eigenvalues CAR_calcEVs3 will produce complex eigenvalues. The possible reason I think is that the matrix is symmetric, but numerically it is not.  I created a new function and specified to evs, which specifies symmetric = TRUE, which seems to solve the problem. 

Below is the example I tried to illustrate this issue.  Then is it possible to use the new nimbleFunction I defined in the nimble code? When I tried to put it in the nimbleCode, it does not work.  And it seems that I cannot specify evs by using a predefined vector? 

Thank you!

library(nimble)
library(Matrix)
library(mvtnorm)
nr = nc = 5
cmat.fun <- function(nr,nc)
{
  # input is the dimension of the grid 
  N <- nr*nc
  index.mat <- matrix(0, N, 4)
  index.mat[,1] <- (1:N) - nr
  index.mat[,2] <- (1:N) - 1
  index.mat[,3] <- (1:N) + 1
  index.mat[,4] <- (1:N) + nr
  index.mat[(index.mat <0) | (index.mat > N)] <- 0
  index.mat[(nr*(1:(nr-1))+1),2] <- 0
  index.mat[nr*(1:nr),3] <- 0
  
  Cmat <- Matrix(0, N, N)
  for (i in 1:N)
  {
    Cmat[i,c(index.mat[i,],i)] <- 1
  }
  return(Cmat)
}

W <- cmat.fun(nr,nc)  
diag(W) <- 0
W <- as.matrix(W)

tau = 1
rho = 0.95
ns = ncol(W)
Dmat = diag(colSums(W))
sp = rmvnorm(1,rep(0,ns),tau*solve(Dmat-rho*W))


adj = unlist(lapply(1:ncol(W), function(x){which(W[x,]==1)}))
num = colSums(W)

dcar_proper(sp, mu = rep(1,length(sp)),adj = adj, num = num, tau = 1, 
            gamma = 0.95, log = TRUE) ### does not work


CAR_calcEVs4 <- nimbleFunction(
  name = 'CAR_calcEVs4',
  run = function(C = double(1), adj = double(1), num = double(1)) {
    Cmatrix <- CAR_calcCmatrix(C, adj, num)
    evs <- eigen(Cmatrix, only.values = TRUE,symmetric = TRUE)$values
    returnType(double(1))
    return(evs)
  }
)


weights <- rep(1,length(adj))
CM <- as.carCM(adj, weights, num)
C = CM$C
M = CM$M

dcar_proper(sp, mu = rep(1,length(sp)),adj = adj, num = num, tau = 1, 
            gamma = 0.95, evs = CAR_calcEVs4(C, adj, num), log = TRUE)

messages.author: c9e9cbbfb3b043f0
messages.subject: Re: dcar_proper: nimEigen() has a complex eigenvalue.
parts:
Xin, thanks for your interest in nimble.

I spent a bit of time looking into your example, and indeed the nimEigen() function, just the same as R's eigen() function, both incorrectly give complex eigenvalues for your inputs.  And indeed, by providing the argument symmetric=TRUE to eigen(), you can get around these numerical issues to correctly calculate the eigenvalues for your adjacency structure.

If you pre-calculate the correct eigenvalues, as you did, you can provide them for the dcar_proper distribution in a nimble model.  I'm assuming that's what you want to do: use the dcar_proper distribution inside a model, with the correct eigen values that you calculated.  Assuming that's the case, I've shown how to do that using your example code and adjacency structure below.  This use of the dcar_proper distribution inside a model, using your pre-calculated eigenvalues, could then be incorporated into a larger model structure, perhaps where sp instead represents a latent spatial variable.

Code is below, please let us know if this solves your problem.

library(nimble)
library(Matrix)
library(mvtnorm)

nr <- nc <- 5

cmat.fun <- function(nr,nc) {
    # input is the dimension of the grid
    N <- nr*nc
    index.mat <- matrix(0, N, 4)
    index.mat[,1] <- (1:N) - nr
    index.mat[,2] <- (1:N) - 1
    index.mat[,3] <- (1:N) + 1
    index.mat[,4] <- (1:N) + nr
    index.mat[(index.mat <0) | (index.mat > N)] <- 0
    index.mat[(nr*(1:(nr-1))+1),2] <- 0
    index.mat[nr*(1:nr),3] <- 0
##

Cmat <- Matrix(0, N, N)
    for (i in 1:N) {
            Cmat[i,c(index.mat[i,],i)] <- 1
        }
    return(Cmat)
}

W <- cmat.fun(nr,nc)  
diag(W) <- 0
W <- as.matrix(W)

tau <- 1
rho <- 0.95
ns <- ncol(W)
Dmat <- diag(colSums(W))
set.seed(0)   ## new -DT
sp <- rmvnorm(1,rep(0,ns),tau*solve(Dmat-rho*W))

adj <- unlist(lapply(1:ncol(W), function(x){which(W[x,]==1)}))
num <- colSums(W)

## not necessary -DT
##CAR_calcEVs4 <- nimbleFunction(
##    name = 'CAR_calcEVs4',
##    run = function(C = double(1), adj = double(1), num = double(1)) {
##        returnType(double(1))
##        return(evs)
##    }
##)

weights <- rep(1, length(adj))
CM <- as.carCM(adj, weights, num)

C <- CM$C
M <- CM$M

Cmatrix <- CAR_calcCmatrix(C, adj, num)
evs <- eigen(Cmatrix, only.values = TRUE, symmetric = TRUE)$values

dcar_proper(sp, mu = rep(1,length(sp)), adj = adj, num = num, tau = 1,
            gamma = 0.95, evs = evs, log = TRUE)
## -24.8071

code <- nimbleCode({
    sp[1:N] ~ dcar_proper(mu=mu0[1:N], C=C[1:L], adj=adj[1:L], num=num[1:N], M=M[1:N], tau=1, gamma=0.95, evs=evs[1:N])
})

N <- length(num)
L <- length(adj)

constants <- list(mu0 = rep(1,N), C = C, adj = adj, num = num, M = M, N = N, L = L, evs = evs)
data <- list(sp = sp[1,])
inits <- list()

Rmodel <- nimbleModel(code, constants, data, inits)

## uncompiled execution
Rmodel$calculate()
## -24.8071

Cmodel <- compileNimble(Rmodel)

## compiled execution
Cmodel$calculate()
## -24.8071
